S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
examples: Constantly shaking legs or twisting and squirming body while seated.
Spinning a pen or fiddling with nearby objects, unable to keep hands still.
Continually changing posture and feeling uncomfortable while sitting.
Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
examples: Frequently leaves seat or wanders around during class or meetings using excuses.
Unable to sit still during meals and keeps getting up.
Leaves seat in the middle of a movie or performance to go to the restroom or go outside.
Continually leaves seat and wanders around in the office where one is expected to sit and work.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
examples: Talks incessantly and cannot tolerate silence, continuing to chatter.
Continues to talk even when others are bored or try to cut the conversation short.
Talks too much inappropriately for the situation, making people around them uncomfortable.
Monopolizes the conversation and gives almost no chance for others to speak.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
examples: Butts into conversations of others where they have not been invited.
Joins in on others' work or games without permission or interferes.
Touches or uses other people's belongings or work without permission.
Keeps talking to and disturbing others when they are focusing on work or studying.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation) is characterized by developmentally inappropriate levels of motor activity, restlessness, talkativeness, and impulsive behaviors, with comparatively fewer or less impairing inattentive symptoms. Individuals often display difficulty remaining seated, acting without considering consequences, interrupting others, and feeling internally driven to be constantly active, leading to problems in school, work, or social settings. Onset is typically in childhood, but functional impairment may become more prominent or clinically recognized only when environmental demands increase, such as in higher education or complex jobs. It is differentiated from anxiety, mood, and substance-related disorders by the pervasive, long-standing pattern of hyperactive-impulsive behavior across settings and by the absence of episodic mood changes or primary substance effects as the central cause.

patient.personality: Maritza is a free-spirited, curious, and hardworking young woman who thrives on movement, novelty, and hands-on problem-solving out on the road.
patient.stressor: Maritza’s symptoms became clinically significant after she transitioned from casual local delivery work during high school to full-time regional trucking with tighter schedules and longer solo drives. The expectation to sit still for hours, follow strict safety protocols, and manage paperwork at distribution centers clashed sharply with her natural drive to keep moving, chatting, and constantly doing something. Over about eight months, dispatchers and supervisors began documenting concerns about her restlessness at loading docks, difficulty staying put during mandatory safety briefings, and impulsive behavior at customer sites, which led to formal warnings and near loss of a key contract. When her company required her to meet with an occupational health provider after a complaint from a warehouse manager about her inability to remain in designated areas, she agreed to a psychiatric referral, worried that what she had always seen as just being “high-energy” was now putting her job and long-term dream of owning a logistics firm at risk.
patient.chief_complaint: “I feel like I can’t ever just sit still on the job, like I’m always on the move even when I’m supposed to be waiting.”

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
S010.manifestation: Any time I’m sitting—behind the wheel, in a safety meeting, even at home on the couch—my leg is bouncing, my fingers are drumming on something, or I’m twisting my badge or the keys, and half the time people have to ask me to stop because it’s so constant and distracting.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
S011.manifestation: When they tell us to stay seated in the break room or the little safety classroom, I last maybe five minutes before I’m up pretending I need more coffee or to use the bathroom, just so I can walk around because my body feels like it’s crawling out of the chair.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
S013.manifestation: I can’t even just chill quietly—if I try to watch a movie with my cousins or sit in the truck waiting for a dock to open, I end up talking, humming, tapping on stuff, or scrolling and commenting out loud, and everybody’s like, ‘Can you just be quiet for one minute?’ and I honestly don’t know how.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
S014.manifestation: It feels like there’s this motor in me that never shuts off, so even after a long run when I’m supposed to rest at the truck stop, I’m pacing the lot, reorganizing my cab, checking the load three times, starting little tasks one after another instead of just sitting still.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
S015.manifestation: Once I start talking, I just go and go—about the route, my plans, random stories from other deliveries—and I catch myself rambling through the whole safety briefing or monopolizing the conversation in the dispatch office until I notice people looking annoyed or trying to cut me off.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
S018.manifestation: I’m always jumping into other people’s conversations at the warehouse or cutting in when dispatch is on the phone, finishing their sentences or answering questions that weren’t even to me, and I don’t realize I’ve interrupted until they give me that look or tell me, ‘Hang on, Maritza, I’m not done yet.’
